length.text: Usually about 60 cm; up to 122 cm

overview.text: The Texas Coral Snake is a brightly ringed, venomous coral snake of the southern United States and Mexico. It is shy and secretive, but its bite is dangerous.

identification.text: Rings of black, yellow and red that go right around the body, onto the belly. Smooth scales, a rounded head and round pupils.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Most are around 60 cm (24 in); the largest reach 122 cm. Males are usually smaller.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Arkansas, Louisiana and Texas in the USA, and north-eastern and central Mexico.

behaviour.text: Shy and mostly active at night, hiding in leaf litter and under logs; sometimes seen moving about after heavy rain. If grabbed it may thrash and bite.

behaviour.label: Bites
behaviour.text: Its fixed front fangs can deliver a lot of venom in a quick bite, so it must never be handled.

diet.text: Mainly other snakes, especially small burrowing ones, but even copperheads and other coral snakes; sometimes small lizards.

recognise.text: Red, yellow and black rings all the way round the body.
